must_remember: Absorption of a thermal neutron by $^{235}\text{U}$ produces an excited compound nucleus $^{236}\text{U}^*$ which undergoes asymmetric fission, releasing ~200 MeV and an average of 2.4 to 2.5 fast neutrons.
Fermi's Four-Factor Formula for an infinite medium is given by $k_{inf} = \epsilon \cdot p \cdot f \cdot \eta$.
For a finite reactor, leakage must be factored in, yielding the effective multiplication factor $k_{eff} = k_{inf} \cdot L_f \cdot L_t$.
Reactivity is defined as $\rho = \frac{k_{eff} - 1}{k_{eff}}$, where $\rho = 0$ corresponds to critical ($k_{eff} = 1$), $\rho > 0$ to supercritical, and $\rho < 0$ to subcritical.
Delayed neutrons (~0.65% for $^{235}\text{U}$) extend the effective generation time, making reactor control feasible.
Good moderators require a high scattering cross-section $\sigma_s$, a low absorption cross-section $\sigma_a$, and a large logarithmic energy decrement $\xi$.

glossary.meaning: The ratio of thermal neutrons produced in generation $(n+1)$ to those in generation $(n)$ in an infinite medium.
The ratio of total neutrons in one generation to the total in the preceding generation in a finite reactor, incorporating leakage.
The fraction of thermal neutrons absorbed in the nuclear fuel compared to all thermal neutrons absorbed in the core.
The probability that a fast neutron slows down to thermal energies without being captured in resonance absorption peaks of fertile nuclei.
The ratio of total fast neutrons produced by fissions at all energies to the fast neutrons produced by thermal fissions alone.
The average number of fast fission neutrons produced per thermal neutron absorbed in the fuel.
The square root of the sum of the thermal diffusion area ($L_t^2$) and the Fermi age ($\tau$), representing the total slowing down and diffusion distance.
